name: Dario Flint
life: Dario's cart is the second business he has owned. The first failed because he never charged friends. He has devised elaborate small jobs children can do in return for treats, a system nobody mistakes for sound accounting. On Sunday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Dario checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I let children freeze the turrets in my cart. They kept opening the lid and my stock softened. I sold the soft ones cheap and put their names on the receipts as architects.
appearance: Dario has a center part and straight chestnut hair, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. When somebody else has the floor, Dario leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Dario thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Dario sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To replace the softened stock without charging the children for their turrets.
family: Stella Hull is Dario’s second cousin. A relative kept reporting household news on postcards long after everybody could afford to phone. Reading one takes the family back to an ordinary morning rather than a big event. Dario prefers an ordinary request to a grand declaration of affection. Asked about *The sheltered corner*, Stella says, “My wheelchair fits the new turn. I brought the planners cake and asked them to hear the old riders too.”
connections: Ada Firth. Turrets from the ice cart and flags from the old competition meet in the families' photograph.
